text:
maria: Quick playback from this morning's selector sweep — hitting a weird slow path for narrow heads that I haven't seen before. microbench on sm90 + sm86, head_dim=12/16, seqlen=64 shows the picker flipping to flashv3 and latency jumping under microbatching.

bench-bot: perf-suite: results uploaded https://internal/bench/3501234567 (summary attached) :chart_with_upwards_trend:

kevin: ugh. do you have the selector debug log? want to see the scoring that caused the flip.

maria: paste below — kept it minimal: 
```
[2026-03-18T09:02:11Z] kernel_picker input: model=redwood-tiny, seqlen=64, head_dim=12, batch=2, device=sm90
[2026-03-18T09:02:11Z] heuristics: seq_bucket=64, head_bucket=12, kvcached=false, thermal_score=0.45
[2026-03-18T09:02:11Z] candidate flashv3 score=0.82 (prefetch_cost=0.12, warp_util=0.7)
[2026-03-18T09:02:11Z] candidate sdpa_v2 score=0.71 (l2_spill_risk=0.05, vectorize_eff=0.88)
[2026-03-18T09:02:11Z] selected=flashv3
[2026-03-18T09:02:11Z] measured: flashv3 latency=11.2ms, sdpa_v2 latency=5.0ms
```

olga: whoa measured is the opposite of scores. is that from an isolated run or within normal traffic? looks like the scoring underestimates L2 thrashing.

maria: isolated repeatable on our microprobe harness. toggling kvcache on/off changes thing — with kvcache warm (recently used keys) the picker still favors flashv3 and it's slower.

tj: possible causes: 1) flashv3 prefetch path for tiny head dims causes unaligned loads -> extra instructions; 2) batcher is coalescing requests with different seqlens causing padding and inflating effective seqlen; 3) L2 footprint for flashv3 grows nonlinearly at small head widths due to frag packets.

kevin: can you capture perf counters? L2 miss rate, local memory allocs, and register spill counts would be good. if flashv3 is spilling registers for head_dim=12 it could be huge.

maria: added perf snippet from sm90 run: 
```
L2_MISS_RATE=0.42
L1_LOCAL_HIT=0.76
REG_SPILLS=18k/s
GLOBAL_MEM_TXNS=120k/s
ukernel_stalls=12%
```
sdpa_v2 run for same config: 
```
L2_MISS_RATE=0.12
REG_SPILLS=3k/s
GLOBAL_MEM_TXNS=60k/s
ukernel_stalls=3%
```

olga: that's convincing. selector's cost model clearly isn't modeling register pressure for flashv3 at tiny head dims. scoring weights probably tuned on head_dim>=32.

kevin: quick mitigation: add a hard rule: if head_dim < 20 and seqlen <= 128, prefer sdpa family unless telemetry shows clear advantage. also add a hysteresis window so we don't flip on transient KV warmup signals.

maria: filed runtime ticket RNW-1842 and pushed a canary flag to dev that forces sdpa_v2 for head_dim<=16 on sm90. canary id: sdpa-narrowheads-2026-03-18.

tj: long term we should: 1) extend the cost model with a small-head register-pressure term; 2) run a sweep across architectures (sm86/89/90) and microbatch sizes to learn a small decision tree; 3) consider adding a microprobe that stresses KV warmup permutations because that seems to move the selector.

maria: i'll own the microprobe and add perf counters to the telemetry event we log at selection time. also plan to add a tiny offline autotune job that fits a corrective multiplier for head_dim<32.

olga: sounds good. minimal follow-ups: - add unit test where head_dim=12 seqlen=64 must prefer sdpa unless explicit override - add metric to alert if selector's chosen kernel is >2x slower than runner's best measured kernel in last 24h

kevin: +1. also make sure the rollout is gated by per-region telemetry — don't flip prod globally overnight.

maria: noted. i'll update RNW-1842 with conservative rollout plan and PR for a quick fix.

tj: FYI i bumped the kernel-picker doc with a note about tiny heads and register pressure (internal link: docs/kernel-picker/narrow-heads).

maria: thanks everyone. will post follow-up with before/after numbers once canary runs for a day. :thumbsup:
